title: Faith and Truth - Episode 2: Walking by faith

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Faith and Truth. <short pause> I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking a simple question... <short pause> what does it mean to walk by faith? <long pause>
The eleventh chapter of Hebrews opens with one of the most famous definitions in all of Scripture. <short pause>
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Faith is the substance of things hoped for... <short pause> the evidence of things not seen. <long pause>
Those words have been painted on church walls and embroidered on cushions for centuries. <short pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: But what do they actually mean for you tonight... here in the quiet, with the day behind you, and your mind too tired to strain after certainty? <long pause>

The word substance means something solid... something you can lean on. <short pause> Faith isn't a feeling you work up inside yourself. It's not a mood, or a surge of confidence. <short pause> It's putting your weight on something outside yourself... on someone who holds you, whether you feel it or not. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Think of a chair. <short pause> You don't sit down because you feel certain about the chair. <short pause> You sit down... and the chair holds you. <long pause>
That's faith. <short pause> You rest your weight on God... and he is the substance, the solid thing. <long pause>

The passage says faith is also the evidence of things not seen. <short pause> Evidence means proof, but not the kind you can photograph or measure. It's the kind of proof that comes from trust. <long pause>

A child in the dark reaches for a parent's hand. <short pause> She can't see the hand... but when her fingers close around it, that's her evidence. <short pause> She knows she's not alone. <long pause>
The next verse tells us something important. <short pause>
For by it the elders obtained a good report. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: By faith, the elders obtained a good report. <short pause> Not by sight, <short pause> not by feeling, <short pause> not by perfect understanding. <short pause> By faith. <long pause>
All those men and women who walked with God before us did so in the same way you can tonight. <short pause> They trusted him... in the dark. <long pause>
Then the writer of Hebrews does something unexpected. <short pause> He takes us back to the very beginning... to the foundation of everything. <long pause>
Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God. <short pause> The things we see were not made of things which do appear. <long pause>
God spoke... and the universe came into being. <short pause> He made everything out of nothing. <long pause>
You can't see that with your eyes, or prove it in a laboratory. <short pause> You understand it... by faith. <long pause>

And if God spoke the stars into existence, if he made the mountains and the oceans with a word... <short pause> then he can hold you tonight. <short pause> He can carry what you can't carry. <long pause>

The next few verses show us Abel, Enoch, and Noah... each one walking by faith in his own generation. <short pause> Abel brought an offering that pleased God. <short pause> Enoch walked with God, and was taken up. <short pause> Noah built an ark when there was no sign of rain. <long pause>
None of them had the whole picture. <short pause> None of them saw the end from the beginning. <short pause> They simply took the next step... in trust. <long pause>
And then comes a verse that matters very much. <short pause>
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Without faith it is impossible to please God. <short pause> For he that cometh to God must believe that he is... <short pause> and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. <long pause>
This is not a threat. <short pause> It's a description of how things are. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You come to God by believing that he is there, and that he is good. <short pause> You don't have to feel it perfectly. You don't have to talk yourself into certainty. <short pause> You just have to turn toward him... like turning your face toward the sun. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Tonight, if your faith feels small... <short pause> that's all right. <short pause> Faith the size of a mustard seed is still faith. <long pause> If you're too tired to feel sure, you can still rest your weight on God. <short pause> He doesn't ask you to hold yourself up. <short pause> He asks you to let him hold you. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Walking by faith means taking one step at a time in his direction. <short pause> It means trusting that he is there, even when you can't see the path ahead. <short pause> And it means knowing that he rewards those who seek him... not because we've earned it, but simply because he is good. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So let that be enough for tonight. <short pause> You don't have to solve every question, or feel every assurance. <short pause> You can close your eyes, and rest in the one who spoke the worlds into being. <long pause>
Let's pray. <long pause> Father, we rest our weight on you tonight. <short pause> Teach us to trust you in the dark... and let us wake knowing we are held. <long pause>
Goodnight.
